A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CALD research, with matching methods, benchmark experiments, and existing figures. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original model-conversion experiments on language and speech tasks in Tables 1-3, plus hidden-state analyses in Figures 3-4.

after.justification: v2 retains the original conversion experiments and adds a qualitative training-from-scratch result and computational-cost measurements.

M1.justification: CALD's architecture replacements, losses, and four guidance modes remain unchanged. Appendix B supplies pseudocode for existing procedures. The added CTC explanation in Section 3 repeats the ASR adaptation already specified in v1 Section 4.4; initialization clarifications do not establish a changed method.

E1.justification: All named training and evaluation datasets and downstream tasks are retained. Appendix C adds an explicit ASR input-length scenario, measuring inference on audio ranging from 10 to 180 seconds; no new corpus is identified.

E2.justification: Tables 1-3 retain their comparator membership. Section 4.4 newly reports an unguided Mamba2 speech model trained without parameter transfer, providing a qualitative from-scratch control beyond the existing parameter-transfer-only baseline.

E3.justification: Table 4 revises unguided learning rates for QNLI/QQP/SST2/IMDB from 1e-4/1e-4/1e-4/3e-4 to 1e-5/1e-5/3e-5/1e-5, and RoBERTa's QNLI/SST2 rates from 1e-5 to 3e-5. These reported setting changes do not establish which experiments were rerun. v2 also introduces the no-transfer control and an audio-length latency evaluation.

E4.justification: v2 adds an ablation removing parameter transfer, reporting unstable speech-model training and poor convergence. Appendix C adds comparisons of computational costs across guidance modes and inference scaling with audio length. The existing hidden-state distance and trajectory analyses are unchanged.

E5.justification: Figure 5 newly specifies averaging inference timings over five runs. This concerns the added timing experiment, not additional training seeds for existing accuracy results. No confidence intervals, variability estimates, or significance tests are added.

E6.justification: Table 1 substantially revises the unguided baseline: QNLI accuracy changes from 53.1% to 69.4%, QQP from 73.3% to 84.3%, SST2 from 82.6% to 83.6%, and average accuracy from 72.9% to 80.0%, materially narrowing CALD's reported advantage under revised learning rates. Table 2 replaces the 1%-Pile hybrid row, changing its average from 0.514 to 0.519. v2 also adds previously absent training-time and inference-scaling results in Appendix C, plus the qualitative from-scratch failure. Table 3 and Figures 3-4 remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions and Equations 1-7 are unchanged. The added pseudocode expresses existing training procedures without adding theoretical assumptions, propositions, proofs, or derivations.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same contributions: joint conversion and fine-tuning through CALD, alternative guidance modes, broad speech/language applicability, and performance approaching the original models. Added efficiency measurements support these existing claims.

C2.justification: v2 explains why initialization from the target teacher should ease distillation and connects hybrid guidance's speech benefits to allowing greater deviation from initial features. It also interprets the new scratch-training failure as evidence for pretraining's necessity. Appendix C discusses computation-performance tradeoffs and qualifies practical speedups as implementation-dependent.

D1.justification: Appendix B adds training pseudocode, Table 4 newly discloses unguided projection-sharing choices, and Section 4.1 clarifies Mamba/Mamba2 initialization. Appendix C provides hardware and runtime information, including 1.6 days for ASR conversion on one 24GB RTX3090. These expand documentation of existing methods; code-access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to parameter transfer, distillation, and conversion during pretraining remain the same. New citation occurrences reuse existing references, while bibliography changes concern capitalization and venue wording.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendices B and C, localized explanatory passages, and corrected figure references, including references to Figures 1-4. The main section order, terminology, and most prose remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds the latency bar chart in Figure 5 and three formatted algorithm blocks. Table 4 gains an unguided sharing-mode row and moves from amid the references into the appendix material. Existing Figures 1-4 and the structures of Tables 1-3 are retained.

improvement.justification: The added pseudocode, explicit implementation settings, and measured computational costs improve reproducibility and give the efficiency argument concrete support. The core method and principal findings remain stable. The gain is limited because the new scratch-training evidence is qualitative and the PDFs do not explain whether replaced scores and settings reflect corrections or reruns.
